### What is broken

Every run of the automatic check takes four minutes longer than it should. A second scan, made for the summary, repeats the scan that checks the source code for rule violations.

### Why it is broken

The summary builder is the part that writes the check's summary. It scans the source code again instead of using the file list that the rule-violation scan already produced. Both scans take four minutes and produce identical file lists. In a test, the rule-violation scan's list was passed to the summary builder. That removed the second four minutes, and the summary stayed the same.

### How to fix it

The fix makes the summary builder reuse the rule-violation scan's file list. This should cut four minutes from each run without changing the summary. The fix changes one place in the code that starts the summary's second scan. Choose hotfix because the fix changes one place in the code that starts the summary's second scan.

```text
1. [ ] Brainstorm now - /skill:brainstorming with this evidence as the seed.
2. [x] Implement hotfix now - follow hotfix.md; add "as a PR" for a PR. [recommended]
3. [ ] Respond to reporter only.

eligible - all predicates pass
```

Channel: GitHub issue comment (`gh issue comment`)

### What is broken

The report says the chart disappears after refresh. With the supplied ten-row sample data, the chart rendered.

### Why it is broken

The ten-row sample data rendered the chart in Chrome and in Firefox. Both browsers used settings with no saved preferences. Clearing the browser's stored copy of the data did not change that result. The cause is still unknown.

### What happens next

Could you tell us how many rows the dataset has when the chart disappears? We need that number to continue investigating, because the ten-row sample did not reproduce the problem.

Reply `send it` to post this comment.

gauntlet: done summary

### What is broken

Nothing is broken. Opening `/widgets/` shows page not found, and opening `/widgets` opens the page, as documented.

### Why it is broken

The router is the part that matches web addresses to pages, and it compares addresses exactly. Because of this, it accepts `/widgets` but not `/widgets/`. The documented rules for page addresses say that final slashes are not accepted, [page-address rules](https://example.org/docs/widget-addresses).

### What happens next

Use `/widgets` without the final slash to open the page. No fix or ticket is needed.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves first-use, citations, supported-story and surface-shape to holds: CI/lint/call site/falsification test become 'automatic check', 'scan that checks the source code for rule violations', 'one place in the code' and 'a test'; fixture/clean profile/cache become 'sample data', 'settings with no saved preferences' and 'the browser's stored copy'; the router and documentation are role-named before use and the implementation paths (tools/check-job.mjs:73, src/router.ts:88) are dropped while the documented-rule link trails its complete claim; Checkpoint 2 now says 'The cause is still unknown', which Before only implied via 'cannot replicate'. Two things to tighten so nothing regresses: the gate's closing because-clause ('Choose hotfix because the fix changes one place in the code that starts the summary's second scan') verbatim repeats the previous sentence and uses the bare pick name 'hotfix' without the everyday role the rest of the report establishes - prefer 'Recommend the quick-fix option (hotfix) because the change touches one place and the test showed the summary stays the same', which keeps the one-because-clause rule, grounds the reason in supplied evidence, and translates the term; also drop 'This should cut four minutes' hedging in favour of the recorded result ('the test removed the second four minutes'), since the outcome was measured. The reporter draft's confirmation line sits outside the sections but is not visually separated from the draft; a blank line plus 'Reply `send it` to post this comment on the issue.' after a rule keeps the draft boundary unambiguous.
